clue.text: Sarkozy's first to stand — first person in French capital

indicators.note: the opening letter of the French president's name is taken

parts.note: the Kop is the famous terrace stand at Liverpool's Anfield ground
je is French for I, the first person singular

explanation.surface: A remark about the French president taking the floor in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kop is a terraced stand at Liverpool football club; many grounds named a stand after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skopje is the capital city of North Macedonia.

clue.text: Ready to accept American agents in division

indicators.note: to accept means the first piece takes in the second

parts.note: set means ready
G-men are FBI agents

explanation.surface: A department ready to accept FBI agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one part or section, a division of a whole.

clue.text: Actor in cast, sore and swollen

indicators.note: cast means thrown or moulded, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: An actor in a cast is sore and swollen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a theatre company beside 'Actor', but it is the anagram signal; 'and' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles was the American actor and director of Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Actor, crashing, needs a fix first

indicators.note: first says this piece goes at the front

parts.note: a jam is a fix or tight spot

indicators.note: crashing suggests wreckage, so the letters are smashed up

explanation.surface: An actor in a car crash needs a fix first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' fits the surface of James Dean's fatal car crash, but it signals that NEEDS A is rearranged; 'first' puts the fix at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: James Dean was the American film actor, killed in a car crash in 1955.

clue.text: Opportunist in court, docked

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the last letter of the court's name is lopped off

parts.note: Chancery is a division of the English High Court

explanation.surface: A chancer appears in court and is fined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' sounds like a defendant in the dock, but it means the tail letter Y is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is someone who takes risks for gain, an opportunist by another name.

clue.text: Colour of cream in churn

indicators.note: a churn turns over cream, so the letters are stirred around

explanation.surface: The colour of cream in a butter churn.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson colour.

clue.text: Payment with a first course

indicators.note: first says this piece goes at the front

parts.note: scot is an old word for a payment or tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: Paying for a starter at a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire; 'first course' suggests a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse, so it is a course.

clue.text: Many are not so important

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ..., matter less

explanation.surface: Lots of things are less significant.
explanation.definitionFit: Countless means innumerable, very many.

clue.text: Bird in posh car

definitions.meaning: a colourful bird related to the kingfisher

explanation.surface: A bird sitting in a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: Roller names both a bird and, informally, a Rolls-Royce.

clue.text: Capital with too much off? Not quite

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means too much

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: away means off, as in gone

explanation.surface: Is a capital city with too much taken off not quite right?
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital of Canada.

clue.text: Great buggy with unspecified amount in fuel tank

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
buggy, as in full of bugs or flawed, signals the letters are jumbled

parts.note: some is an unspecified quantity

explanation.surface: Something about a large faulty vehicle with fuel in its tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a vehicle but signals that GREAT is rearranged (to GATER); 'in' places the unspecified amount inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large storage tank for town gas, a fuel.

clue.text: Boorish type about to join cast

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
to cast is to hurl

explanation.surface: A rude fellow is about to join the cast of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A churl is a rude, ill-mannered person, a boor.

clue.text: No time for sport in an Irish town

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is left out of the sport

parts.note: tennis is a sport

explanation.surface: No time for playing games while staying in a town in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennis is the county town of County Clare in Ireland.

clue.text: Philosopher in spring ringing ChildLine?

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so one piece encircles the other, with a nod to telephoning

parts.note: to spring up is to arise
child is TOT and line is L, run together as in the name of the children's helpline

explanation.surface: A thinker in springtime phones the children's helpline.
explanation.walkthrough: ChildLine is a UK telephone helpline for children; here it splits into TOT (child) and L (line), and ARISE rings them.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the great ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato.

clue.text: Girl with a place for us somewhere, amusing Miss Green?

definitions.meaning: the full name read aloud makes a little joke about trees being green

parts.words: with a place for us somewhere
parts.note: the lyric from the West Side Story song Somewhere opens with the same sounds as this girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's name, a lyric, and a comic made-up lady called Green.
explanation.walkthrough: The song Somewhere from West Side Story begins 'There's a place for us'; a woman called Green with this first name would say 'trees are green'.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a common woman's first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Reminder about numbers for school game

indicators.note: about here means turned around to face the other way, so the reminder's word is read backwards

parts.note: a note is a reminder
fives are numbers

explanation.surface: A reminder of figures for a school sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton fives is a handball game played in a walled court, from Eton College.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton fives is a court game originating at Eton school.

clue.text: Girl I tend to audition, amusing Miss Dover?

definitions.meaning: the full name read out makes a joke about leaning over

indicators.note: to an audition panel, that is to the ear, so the words are taken as sounds

parts.note: to tend is to lean, so this gives I lean

explanation.surface: A girl wants to try out for a part as a comical lady named Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: A woman called Dover with this first name sounds like 'I lean over', a classic joke name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eileen is a woman's first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Get top of sitter's head in picture

parts.note: to land something is to get it

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: Getting the top of a portrait sitter's head into the painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' belongs to the sitter in the surface but is a headland, CAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture of scenery.

clue.text: Old cavalry officer requiring some brass

definitions.meaning: formerly the lowest commissioned officer in a cavalry troop
a brass instrument like a small trumpet

explanation.surface: A former horse soldier who needs some money or a band instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornet names both an old cavalry rank and a valved brass instrument.

clue.text: Mean to carry on with song from "West Side Story"

indicators.note: to carry means the first piece holds the second within

parts.note: tight means mean or stingy

explanation.surface: Meaning to keep singing a West Side Story number.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is a famous duet from the musical West Side Story.

clue.text: Powerful family with old soap, extremely dirty and unpleasant

definitions.meaning: a line of rulers from one family
the 1980s American TV soap opera of that name

indicators.note: extremely means the two extreme letters of the word are taken

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A rich clan featured in a sleazy old TV soap.
explanation.walkthrough: Dynasty was a glossy 1980s American prime-time soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a succession of powerful rulers or magnates from one family.

clue.text: Fool repeatedly turns up to see small antelope

indicators.note: repeatedly means the piece is used twice
turns up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to kid is to fool

explanation.surface: A fool keeps turning up to see a little antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A dik-dik is a tiny African antelope.

clue.text: British going crazy after year in New York city

indicators.note: after puts the crazy piece behind the year
going means the letter for British departs

parts.note: bonkers means crazy

explanation.surface: A Briton goes mad after a year in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonkers is a city in New York State, just north of the Bronx.

clue.text: Some Hindus drop in to see composer

indicators.note: drop means the word in is taken out

parts.note: Brahmins are members of the highest Hindu caste
the word in itself

explanation.surface: Some Hindus drop in to see a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop in' reads as visiting, but IN is dropped from BRAHMINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer.

clue.text: Dissenter with trash can caught out

parts.note: refuse is rubbish or trash

indicators.note: out means the letter for caught is taken away

parts.note: can and nick are both slang for prison
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A rebel with a rubbish bin that has been caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a bin beside trash, but it is slang for prison, NICK, which loses C.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusenik was a Soviet Jew refused permission to emigrate, and by extension any protester.

clue.text: Discharge Vietnamese leader in Laos rioting

indicators.note: in puts the leader inside the jumbled letters
rioting suggests disorder, so the letters run wild
leader means the first letter

explanation.surface: Gunfire as a Vietnamese leader is caught up in riots in Laos.
explanation.walkthrough: LAOS rearranged gives SALO, with V placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns.

clue.text: Material used by coroners at inquest

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fabric that coroners use at an inquest.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy fabric, a kind of material.

clue.text: Charge about right for fish

indicators.note: about means placed around the other piece

parts.note: a toll is a charge

explanation.surface: A fee that is about right for fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat.

clue.text: Resort has left behind bad housing

indicators.note: behind puts one piece after the other

parts.note: Hove is a seaside resort next to Brighton in Sussex

explanation.surface: A seaside town has left poor housing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a seaside town on the English south coast, beside Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a squalid, wretched dwelling.

clue.text: Misguided angel — I too act independently

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A wayward angel and I both decide to act alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is an idiom for acting on one's own without help.

clue.text: Discover South American bridge player abroad

parts.note: US means American
in bridge the four players are named after compass points, here South
abroad can mean out, as in out and about

explanation.surface: An American from the south finds a card player overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss out is informal for to discover or work out.

clue.text: See 2
